title: Game Math Part 2 · Rendering6: Transforming Normals and UV Mapping

scenes.title: 확대된 표면의 법선과 무늬를 연결하기
lines: What should you check when lighting directions or patterns look wrong after stretching a shape?
First verify normal-tangent perpendicularity and the inverse-transpose rule in a numerical example.
Then inspect game wall and roof patterns and explain UV correspondence, crop, rotation and flipping.
Finally compare repeat and clamp and demonstrate why wrapping vertices before interpolation fails.

scenes.title: 법선은 접선과 수직이어야 합니다
lines: Normals must remain perpendicular to tangents. Use column vectors t and n with n transpose t equal zero.
Let M be the invertible linear transform of positions and tangents; do not add translation to directions.
Transform normals with the inverse transpose M inverse transpose; inverse and transpose commute in this expression.
The transformed dot product cancels M inverse M and equals the original zero dot product, preserving perpendicularity.
For orthogonal rotations the inverse transpose equals M; positive uniform scale preserves the normalized direction.
Nonuniform scale and shear require inverse transpose then normalization; singular zero-axis transforms have no inverse.
Orientation-reversing transforms also require consistent front-face handling; our worked example uses positive scales.

scenes.title: 가로 두 배 확대를 직접 검산하기
lines: Choose tangent(1,−1) and normal(1,1): their dot product1−1 is zero.
Scaling x by two produces tangent(2,−1), changing the surface slope.
Applying M to the normal gives(2,1), whose dot with the new tangent is4−1=3 rather than zero.
Normalizing the wrong vector by square root five leaves dot3 divided by square root five, so its direction remains wrong.
The inverse transpose scales x by one half, giving(.5,1) with transformed dot1−1=0.
Final normalization gives approximately(.447,.894): first correct the perpendicular direction, then normalize.
The same perpendicularity condition extends to3D; distinguish the linear position transform from the normal matrix in lighting code.

scenes.title: 각진 바위와 벽 무늬의 대응 보기
lines: Move among Megabonk rocks and buildings, separating faceted rock surfaces from wall markings.
View changes preserve angular outlines, while face brightness and wall markings motivate lighting and surface-property questions.
The next passage crosses low rocks and sand; the final section alternately reveals building front and side faces.
Windows and strip-like marks appear on faces; we observe their relationship without reading game UVs or texture files.
Our numerical example preserved normal-tangent perpendicularity; next connect separate image coordinates for patterns.
Correct geometry and normals cannot fix lookup of the wrong image region; verify these data roles separately.

scenes.title: 벽돌 무늬와 창문 격자는 어디에서 올까요?
lines: Inspect another Sunset Overdrive roof and wall, where repeated rectangular windows meet a sloped roof.
Observe the large outline first, then internal patterns; abundant detail does not imply one vertex per detail.
The closer wall shows brick-like patterns and grids, motivating correspondence between image locations and surface locations.
We have not inspected game texture files or address modes; the visible patterns motivate separate pattern coordinates.
Our diagram applies an original labeled texture to a four-vertex plate and changes its image mapping while keeping the plate fixed.

scenes.title: 픽셀과 텍셀, 위치와 UV
lines: A texture stores surface color or other attributes; its texels differ from pixels in the final image.
One texel may affect multiple screen pixels when magnified, while multiple texels may contribute to a smaller screen footprint.
Here u runs right and v down, with top-left(0,0) and bottom-right(1,1).
This is an explicit example convention; file row order, tools and transforms matter, so API names alone do not decide orientation.
Normalized0-to1 coordinates cover an image regardless of whether it is8 by8 or larger, independently of3D positions.
Planar, cylindrical and spherical mapping construct the correspondence, authored in tools or computed procedurally at vertices.
Interpolate vertex UVs inside faces, retaining the earlier perspective-correct treatment while focusing on the data being interpolated.

scenes.title: 같은 판에 전체·확대·회전 무늬 붙이기
lines: Imagine pinning cloth to four plate vertices; their selected image locations define the interior correspondence.
Assign(0,0),(1,0),(1,1),(0,1) in order to cover the plate with the entire image without moving vertices.
Restrict both coordinates to.25 through.75, stretching the central half-width and half-height over the plate.
Cycling the UV corners rotates the pattern correspondence rather than rotating the3D plate.
Using1−u flips the image horizontally while preserving geometry positions and face winding.
UVs also apply to multi-triangle meshes, changing placement and stretching without changing their geometry.
The cloth analogy explains correspondence, not physical cloth simulation or guaranteed area preservation.

scenes.title: 무늬는 면을 따라가고 윤곽은 남습니다
lines: Move near a red facade where markings sit within a larger curved form.
View changes alter the apparent pattern orientation and size, reminding us that texture and screen coordinates differ.
The next roof shows repeated strips and glass panes; the container then reveals differently oriented top and side panels.
We do not read these game UVs; the observed pattern-surface relationships motivate our explicitly authored examples.
As with our plate, a surface can map a whole image or a portion; next consider coordinates outside0 through1.
Repeated appearance alone does not prove repeat addressing: separate geometry or repeated content in an image can look similar.

scenes.title: 면 안의 반복 무늬를 따라 관찰하기
lines: Characters move in Big Walk green room; locate the black grid panel and circular wall markings.
Turning views changes the grid apparent angle; screen locations differ from pattern locations on a surface.
As characters approach and move sideways, markings remain associated with their surface regions, motivating texture correspondence.
Repeated shapes do not prove repeat addressing; the repetitions could be contained within the image itself.
The black grid has not been verified as triangle topology; distinguish repeated markings from geometric connections.
Our next diagram uses one original image with explicitly chosen UV spans and addressing, letting us verify the resulting patterns.
Remember to interpolate within the face before texture lookup; we also compare the failure of folding vertex coordinates too early.

scenes.title: 범위 밖의 UV를 조회하는 규칙
lines: UVs can exceed0 through1. Keep vertices and UVs identical while comparing repeat and clamp addressing.
Repeat reuses the image across integer tiles; use u minus floor u consistently for negative coordinates.
For1.25 floor is1, giving.25; for−.75 floor is−1, also giving.25.
Truncating toward zero differs for negative inputs; distinguish floor from truncation when implementing repeat.
Clamp limits below-zero to0 and above-one to1, extending edge values outward.
Mirrored repeat alternates tile orientation, and u and v may use separate address modes.
Addressing selects coordinates independently of filtering, which combines texels; exact edge behavior also depends on those sampling conventions.

scenes.title: 정점에서 먼저 반복하면 정보가 사라집니다
lines: A0-to2 u edge should display two repeats; store the unmodified endpoint coordinates0 and2.
Interpolation gives.5 at one quarter and1.5 at three quarters along the edge.
Applying repeat at lookup maps both positions to.5, the same relative location in different tiles.
Wrapping endpoints0 and2 first turns both into zero, so interpolation loses the entire0-to2 variation.
The two-repeat span is lost; interpolate first and apply addressing only at texture lookup.
Use the preceding perspective-correct UV interpolation before this step; perspective correction and repeat order are separate requirements.

scenes.title: 윤곽·방향·무늬를 나누어 다시 관찰하기
lines: Move among stairs and buildings in Sunset Overdrive, first identifying near and distant surface boundaries.
As roofs and building sides appear, separate three questions: geometry, lighting direction and surface pattern.
The following wall has repeated windows and the roof repeated panels, which do not reveal vertex counts or address modes.
Our calculations used indices for vertex records, normals for perpendicular directions and UVs for image correspondence; their roles differ.
When checking a model, inspect silhouettes, normal boundaries and pattern placement separately to narrow the source of an error.
Finish with explicitly defined mesh exercises that verify storage and calculation order rather than guessing game internals.

scenes.title: 세 가지 질문으로 계산을 검산하기
lines: First exercise: four32-byte vertices and six2-byte indices total140 bytes; distinguish record count from index count.
Second, split a cube corner shading direction by duplicating records and updating the corresponding face indices.
The transformed tangent(2,−1) and normal(.5,1) have zero dot product; verify perpendicularity and unit length after nonuniform scale.
Third, preserve0-to2 UVs for interpolation, repeat at lookup and use floor for negative coordinates.
We separated topology indices, shading normals and UV correspondence; equal positions need not share all attributes.
Next we evaluate lighting with these normals and examine lights and materials; today surface data supplies those inputs.
